extracted.intended_audience: researchers and conference/program chairs designing or analyzing reviewer-assignment algorithms for peer review (machine-learning / CS venues)
extracted.subtask_description: Designing and evaluating algorithms that assign reviewers to papers to maximize a fairness objective (max-min over per-paper summed transformed similarities) while respecting reviewer/paper load constraints and providing statistical guarantees for downstream tasks (e.g., top-k recovery).

rubrics_metrics.name: Max-min fairness objective (Γ_S^f)
rubrics_metrics.description: Fairness objective is the per-paper worst-case measure: for each paper compute the sum (over its assigned reviewers) of f(s_ij) (where f is a monotonically increasing transform of similarities) and the fairness Γ_S^f(A) is the minimum of these per-paper sums across all papers; the goal is to maximize this minimum.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The PeerReview4All algorithm optimizes this objective (or approximates its optimum). All approximation and statistical guarantees in the paper are stated relative to this fairness objective. Use f to reflect how similarity translates to utility (e.g., f(s)=s or f=1−h).

rubrics_metrics.name: Subroutine: maximize minimum similarity via incremental flow construction
rubrics_metrics.description: The subroutine constructs a 4-layer flow network (source → reviewers → papers → sink) and incrementally adds unit-capacity reviewer→paper edges in decreasing order of similarity until a max-flow of size |M|·κ is feasible; when feasible, the assignment using only added edges maximizes the minimum similarity among assigned (reviewer,paper) pairs for that κ.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Edges are added one at a time in order of decreasing sij; after each edge addition check for feasibility (max-flow). This guarantees the output assignment maximizes the lowest similarity in the assignment for the given κ. Integer capacities ensure polynomial-time integer max-flow.

rubrics_metrics.name: Choice among multiple max-flows (heuristics)
rubrics_metrics.description: If multiple max-flows exist when the flow of size |M|κ is reached, the PC can choose any arbitrarily or use heuristics such as selecting the max-flow with maximum cost.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Selecting max-flow with maximum total cost (where costs are similarities) combines fairness with higher average assignment quality; Appendix C describes an alternative choice that helps with topic coverage. Theoretical approximation guarantees hold for any max-flow chosen.

rubrics_metrics.name: Construct candidate assignments for all κ ∈ [λ] and choose highest fairness
rubrics_metrics.description: For each integer κ ∈ [λ], construct an assignment where each paper has κ 'strong' reviewers (via subroutine) and then complement it with λ−κ additional reviewers; produce λ candidate assignments and pick the one with highest fairness (including the assignment from prior iterations).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This step ensures a worst-case fairness guarantee (as in Theorem 1) and lets the algorithm adapt to structure in the similarity matrix (e.g., when some papers have only η strong reviewers).

rubrics_metrics.name: Recursive fixing of most disadvantaged papers (beyond worst-case)
rubrics_metrics.description: After choosing the best candidate assignment in an iteration, identify the most disadvantaged papers (those achieving the minimum per-paper sum) and permanently fix their reviewer assignments; then repeat the procedure on remaining papers to optimize the second worst-off, third worst-off, etc.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Fixing disadvantaged papers prevents later iterations from worsening their allocation and ensures the algorithm optimizes fairness recursively across all papers (Corollary 2).

rubrics_metrics.name: Approximation guarantee (Theorem 1) — multiplicative bound
rubrics_metrics.description: PeerReview4All guarantees a provable lower bound on Γ_S^f(APR4A) relative to the optimal Γ_S^f(A_HARD) given by expressions (7a)/(7b); in particular, the algorithm achieves at least a 1/λ multiplicative approximation in the worst case.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Interpret the formal fraction in (7a) as a tighter bound depending on s*_κ values; when λ=1 the algorithm is exact. The multiplicative nature ensures a non-trivial guarantee even when optimal fairness is small (unlike some additive guarantees).

rubrics_metrics.name: Early stopping guarantee
rubrics_metrics.description: The intermediate assignment produced the first time Step 3 is executed already satisfies the fairness guarantee of Theorem 1.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Program chairs can stop the algorithm after the first outer iteration to save computation while still retaining the same fairness guarantees and associated statistical results.

rubrics_metrics.name: Computational complexity consideration
rubrics_metrics.description: A naïve implementation of PeerReview4All has computational complexity O(λ (m + n) m^2 n) (details and implementation notes in Appendix B).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Consider optimized max-flow implementations and practical engineering (Appendix B) to reduce runtimes for large conferences.

rubrics_metrics.name: Variable reviewer and paper loads support
rubrics_metrics.description: Algorithm supports specifying different maximum loads µ(i) per reviewer and different paper loads λ(j); when using κ as a per-iteration target, set paper→sink capacity to min{κ, λ(j)}.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This generality allows real-world constraints (e.g., reviewers with varying capacities or papers requiring variable numbers of reviewers) to be encoded directly into the flow network.

rubrics_metrics.name: Incorporating conflicts of interest
rubrics_metrics.description: Conflicts of interest are encoded by setting the corresponding similarity sij to −∞ (effectively forbidding that reviewer-paper edge).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Simple and direct way to ensure certain reviewer→paper assignments are impossible within the flow construction.

rubrics_metrics.name: Topic coverage modification
rubrics_metrics.description: After ensuring fairness, techniques (e.g., Long et al., 2013) can be used to pick among approximately fair assignments the one that approximately maximizes the number of distinct topics covered.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Appendix C and referenced methods discuss integrating topic-coverage objectives as a secondary criterion without violating the fairness guarantees.

rubrics_metrics.name: Avoiding LP-relaxation rounding pitfalls (comparison to ILPR / TPMS)
rubrics_metrics.description: LP-relaxation and rounding approaches (e.g., ILPR) can split reviewer capacity fractionally in relaxation and produce poor rounded assignments (e.g., assigning reviewers with zero similarity), whereas the sequential edge-addition prevents assigning papers to weak reviewers and is crucial for the fairness objective.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The paper gives examples and analysis (Section 5.3 and Appendix A.1) showing ILPR can return arbitrarily bad fairness; PeerReview4All's construction avoids such bottlenecks.

rubrics_metrics.name: Objective-score statistical model (scores and noise)
rubrics_metrics.description: Assume each paper j has true quality θ*_j and each reviewer i's score y_ij ~ N(θ*_j, σ^2_ij) with σ^2_ij = h(s_ij) where h is a known monotonically decreasing function mapping similarity to variance.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This model captures reviewer competence varying by reviewer–paper similarity; h can be learned from past data. The model omits reviewer bias (can be handled separately via calibration/post-processing).

rubrics_metrics.name: Estimator: Maximum Likelihood Estimator (MLE)
rubrics_metrics.description: θ^MLE_j = (Σ_{i∈R_A(j)} y_ij / σ^2_ij) / (Σ_{i∈R_A(j)} 1/σ^2_ij) — a weighted average with weights 1/σ^2_ij; under the Gaussian model it is the minimum-variance linear unbiased estimator.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Prefer MLE when model assumptions (noise variances tied to similarities via h) are believed correct; this gives more weight to reviewers expected to be less noisy (higher similarity).

rubrics_metrics.name: Estimator: Mean score (MEAN)
rubrics_metrics.description: θ^MEAN_j = (1/λ) Σ_{i∈R_A(j)} y_ij — the simple average across assigned reviewers.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: MEAN is model-agnostic and empirically robust to model mismatch; often predictive of acceptance decisions and useful when h is unknown or model assumptions are suspect.

rubrics_metrics.name: k-separation threshold (Δ_k) for top-k recovery
rubrics_metrics.description: Define Δ_k = θ*_(k) − θ*_(k+1). This gap between the k-th and (k+1)-th true qualities quantifies difficulty of exactly recovering top-k papers.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Larger Δ_k makes recovery easier; statistical recovery bounds (Theorem 3) are stated in terms of Δ_k, m, λ, q, τ_q and h.

rubrics_metrics.name: Similarity-class S(q) (feasibility of good fairness)
rubrics_metrics.description: Define family S(q) of similarity matrices S such that Γ_S^{1−h}(A_HARD) ≥ q (i.e., the optimal fairness, under f=1−h, is at least q); used to parameterize recovery guarantees.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Constrains the analysis to regimes where satisfactory reviewer coverage exists; q typically lies in [λ(1−h(0)), λ].

rubrics_metrics.name: Approximation quality τ_q
rubrics_metrics.description: τ_q := inf_{S∈S(q)} Γ_S^{1−h}(A_PR4A) / Γ_S^{1−h}(A_HARD) captures the (worst-case over S in S(q)) approximation ratio of PeerReview4All relative to optimal under f=1−h.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Theorem 1 provides lower bounds on τ_q (e.g., ≥1/λ in worst case); τ_q quantifies how algorithmic approximation affects statistical recovery thresholds.

rubrics_metrics.name: Exact top-k recovery condition (Theorem 3)
rubrics_metrics.description: Under bounded h ∈ [0,1], for q in an appropriate range and given τ_q, there is an explicit sufficient condition on Δ_k (gap) — scaling with (λ − q τ_q), ln m, and other factors — guaranteeing that using PeerReview4All plus either MLE or MEAN recovers the true top-k with high probability; a matching converse lower bound is provided.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use the provided inequalities (Theorem 3 parts (a) and (b)) to evaluate whether the combination of assignment algorithm, estimator, and problem difficulty (Δ_k, similarity structure) suffice for reliable top-k recovery.

rubrics_metrics.name: Bounded-noise assumption for analysis
rubrics_metrics.description: For parts of the statistical analysis the paper assumes h: [0,1]→[0,1] (noise variances bounded by 1) which encodes that every reviewer provides at least some minimum competence even at zero similarity.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This normalization simplifies constants; in practice one can rescale h to meet this assumption or handle more general bounded ranges as noted.
